themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 9 this week versus a 2.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 324% increase (z-score: 4.48)—suggesting either seasonal tree stress, disease outbreak, or storm damage requiring immediate Parks Department assessment.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (324% spike)
Z-score of 4.48 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Coincides with overgrown tree/branches complaints also up 374% last week (16 vs. 3.4 avg)
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to determine if disease, pest infestation, or recent weather event is driving cluster
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about visible tree damage or safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Vegetation Problem
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints reached 16 last week—a 374% surge over the 3.4 weekly average (z-score: 10.36)—pointing to either deferred Parks maintenance or unusually rapid seasonal growth in the district.
evidence: 16 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs. 3.4 weekly baseline (374% increase)
Z-score of 10.36 indicates extremely high statistical significance
Convergence signal: also tracking 9 dead/dying tree complaints this week
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department tree maintenance schedule and compare against complaint hotspots
Map complaint locations to identify whether specific blocks or avenues lack regular trimming

themes_detail.label: Encampment Activity Rising
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 8 last week—a 482% increase over the 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.7)—indicating either new homeless encampments or deteriorating conditions at existing sites in the district.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (482% spike)
Z-score of 4.7 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Obstruction complaints also up 209% to 29 last week (vs. 9.4 avg), potentially related to encampment-related blockages
reporting_angles: Locate encampments on street via 311 complaint mapping; conduct fieldwork to document conditions and interview residents
Contact NYPD Outreach and DSNY to understand enforcement response and social services availability

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded to 7 two weeks ago from a 0.2 weekly average—a 2,700% spike (z-score: 15.59)—suggesting either new enforcement activity, illicit vendor activity concentration, or resident frustration with street vending.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (2,700% increase)
Z-score of 15.59 is the most extreme statistical deviation in the dataset
No prior pattern of vendor complaints, making this genuinely new issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Consumer Affairs to determine if compliance action was initiated in Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend
Interview street vendors and residents to understand what prompted surge in complaints

themes_detail.label: Obstruction Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 29 last week—a 209% increase over the 9.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.79)—potentially linked to encampment activity, illegally parked vehicles, or street debris blocking sidewalks and thoroughfares.
evidence: 29 obstruction complaints last week vs. 9.4 weekly average (209% spike)
Z-score of 5.79 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Convergence signal: encampment complaints also up 482% and illegal parking remains highest complaint type (4,311 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference obstruction complaint locations with encampment and illegal parking hotspots to determine primary cause
Document blocked sidewalks via fieldwork; interview residents on accessibility impact
